'''Munduruku''' is a [[Tupian languages|Tupi language]] spoken by 10,000 people in the [[Tapajós|Tapajós River]] basin in north central [[Brazil]].

Gomes (2006) points out that Munduruku is one of the languages of the Tupian family and constitutes, together with [[Kuruaya language|Kuruaya]], the Munduruku linguistic branch [...] The Portuguese language has made significant inroads among the Munduruku but most of the women and children are monolingual. Some loss of the Munduruku language is occurring among those who live in the area of the Madeira River and on the outskirts of the towns next to the Tapajós River; however the situation is not as bad as it seems, as even here the language of the majority is Munduruku and bilingualism arises only after Munduruku has already been acquired (around 10 years of age), usually as a result of learning Portuguese at school.

Those who live in the villages of the Tapajós River valley speak only Munduruku, even in the presence of non-indigenous people. There are elementary schools in almost all villages, and courses promoted by the Brazilian government have turned over education to the Mundurukú, who are starting to take control of their own formal education."<ref name="Gomes">{{Cite thesis |last=Gomes |first=Dioney Moreira |title=Estudo morfológico e sintático da língua mundurukú (tupí) |date=2006 |degree=Doctor's |publisher=Universidade de Brasília |url=http://repositorio.unb.br/bitstream/10482/3754/1/2006_Dioney%20Moreira%20Gomes.pdf |language=pt |trans-title=Morphological and Syntactic Study of the Mundurukú Language (Tupí)}}</ref>

=== Syllable structure ===
The syllable in Munduruku is made up of an obligatory vocalic nucleus and one of four phonemic accents (three of [[Pitch accent|pitch]] and one of laryngealization). It may also have an [[Syllable onset|onset]] or [[Syllable coda|coda]]. No [[consonant cluster]]s are permitted. Thus, the permissible syllables are CV, CVC, V, and VC (with V being the most rare).

==== Onset ====
The onset in this language may be any one of the 16 consonant phonemes which contrast as to the manner and [[point of articulation]]: (1) voiceless stops {{IPA|/p, t, k, tʃ, k, ʔ/}}; (2) voiced stops {{IPA|/b, d dʒ/}}; (3) fricatives {{IPA|/s, ʃ, h/}}; (4) nasals {{IPA|/m, n, ŋ/}}; and (5) sonorants {{IPA|/w, y, r/}}.<ref name="Picanço">{{Cite book |last=Picanço |first=Gessiane Lobato |title=Munduruku: Phonetics, phonology, synchrony, diachrony |publisher=Ann Arbor: University of British Columbia |year=2005}}</ref>

==== Coda ====
The only segment not allowed in the coda is {{IPA|/tʃ/}}. Observe that CVj and CVw and not CV.V ones are considered CVC syllables for a variety of reasons; one is that it would require positing a new syllable pattern limited to CVu and CVi with no other vowels occurring in coda position. There is also a phonetic contrast between {{IPA|/i, u/}} as vowel nuclei and {{IPA|/y, w/}} as codas, the former being distinctly vocalic and the latter consonantal.{{Sfn|Braun|Crofts|1965|p=25}}

==== Nucleus ====
The syllabic nucleus is limited to only one vowel.<ref name="Braun">{{Cite journal |last1=Braun |first1=Ilse |last2=Marjorie Crofts |date=1965 |title=Mundurukú Phonology |journal=Anthropological Linguistics |language=en |volume=7 |issue=7 |pages=23–39 |jstor=30013071}}</ref>

=== Accent ===
Accent is considered a feature of the entire syllable rather than of the nucleus only. One accent occurs with each syllable. Note that the functional load of accent is light—only some 40 lexical pairs with contrastive accents have been found, and few grammatical contrasts are marked by accent alone.{{Sfn|Braun|Crofts|1965|p=27}}
